text:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected — routing/fallback oscillation affecting tenant=apollo. Observed repeated spillover from dedicated pool dp-east-3 into hosted-standard-fallback and back, causing 5xx spike.
pagerduty: paging ajay.k (on-call) — escalation: Sev2. Please ack.
ajay.k: acked. looking now. any customer impact metrics?
maria.pm: csm_linda reported Apollo AI seeing failed requests and degraded p99 latency. They saw ~40% increase in errors starting ~01:12 UTC.
carl.eng: logs show policy engine flipping fallback-policy for tenant=apollo between region=us-east-1 and eu-west-1 due to capacity signals. The fallback rule is configured to let hosted handle spillover but it's reassigning incorrectly.
ajay.k: can we confirm which model variant got routed? suspected wrong variant (gptx-1b-compat vs gptx-1b-quant) causing incompatibility and immediate errors.
carl.eng: yes — dp-east-3 serves gptx-1b-quant. Hosted fallback only supports gptx-1b-compat. We see 502s when requests go to hosted because model signature mismatch in runtime.
tom.ops: that should never happen. tenant isolation policy should prevent mixing dedicated and hosted model families.
dev-platform: reproducing routing trace for a failing request id=rq_8f33c: route path: dp-east-3 -> decision: capacity-tier=hosted fallback -> route to hosted-standard-fallback (gptx-1b-compat). then the request loops back to dp-east-3 because kernel mismatch triggers a retry, causing oscillation.
ajay.k: ok immediate mitigation: temporarily disable fallback for tenant=apollo to prevent spillover to hosted. Run command?
carl.eng: run:
```
redwoodctl routing update --tenant apollo --set fallback.enabled=false --who "ajay.k"
```
maria.pm: pls post confirmation when toggle applied, and tell customer we're putting them into a protected state.
ajay.k: applied toggle. response: 200 OK. fallback.enabled=false for tenant=apollo.
sre-bot: action logged by ajay.k at 1729456920.
ajay.k: monitoring error rate — p50/p95 stable but error rate still elevated due to queued retries. I am draining hosted backlog for apollo and forcing TTLs.
tom.ops: manually purging failing queued requests for tenant apollo:
```
redwoodctl queue purge --tenant apollo --reason "post-fallback disable purge" --who "tom.ops"
```
carl.eng: pushed a temporary policy hotfix to prevent region-based reassignments while fallback is disabled. commit id: 5f9b2.
dev-platform: also set routing debug logs to verbose for dp-east-3 and hosted-standard-fallback. watch for any re-emergence.
maria.pm: CSM notified Apollo support channel. CSM message: "We're investigating a routing/fallback issue causing errors. We've isolated your traffic to your dedicated pool and are purging failing requests. ETA 20-30m."
csm_linda: customer acknowledged, wants periodic updates.
ajay.k: starting controlled canary to re-enable a safer fallback path (compatibility-checked) — will re-enable but force variant mapping to quant-compatible hosted variant (if exists), else keep disabled.
carl.eng: we don't have a hosted quant variant in eu-west-1; that caused the original mismatch when the policy routed by region. we need to avoid region fallback when model families differ.
ajay.k: plan: 1) keep fallback disabled; 2) add policy guard to reject fallback if model_family != model_family; 3) backfill a quant-compatible hosted variant or restrict routing by region/capacity tiers long-term. implementing step 2 now.
```
# policy patch (hotfix)
- condition: fallback.enabled == true
+ condition: fallback.enabled == true AND model_family == target_model_family
```
carl.eng: patch applied at 1729457001. policy engine version bumped.
sre-bot: policy change detected and recorded. rollouts: hotfix -> dp-east-3, hosted-standard-fallback.
maria.pm: status update to customer: "We've implemented a guard to prevent mismatched model-family fallbacks and isolated your traffic to dedicated pool. We'll re-evaluate re-enabling fallback with compatibility checks."
csm_linda: customer requests timeline to full resolution and root cause. They have live production workflows.
ajay.k: handoff: I'm going offline for 30m to restack. handing on-call to tom.ops. leaving monitoring and checklist in thread.
tom.ops: taking over. I'll keep a 10m update cadence. current error rate: down from 40% to 2%. p99 latency back near baseline.
ajay.k: thanks — noted. If error stays <5% for 15m we can move to post-incident review.
dev-platform: recorded request traces and will attach to postmortem. flagged cluster telemetry: dp-east-3 kernel mismatch detection missed because signature comparison was only enabled for offline QA routes. adding runtime assert ticket.
carl.eng: root cause summary (preliminary): routing policy allowed region fallback even when model_variants were incompatible; capacity-tier spillover logic didn't check model_family alignment; tenant isolation guard failed when hot-rebalance occurred across pools.
maria.pm: impact summary for postmortem: Apollo (tenant id ap-428) experienced ~22k failed requests, peak 5xx rate 42% for 18 minutes, one customer-facing outage banner; billing unaffected.
ajay.k: severity review: downgrade to Sev3 for SLAs after mitigation but keep internal incident record and postmortem.

sre-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED for paging purposes — mitigation actions applied, handoff complete. Please add follow-up action items in postmortems channel.

tom.ops: adding three action items now: 1) policy guard ✅ (deployed), 2) add compat checks to routing decision (PR 4321), 3) create hosted quant variant or block cross-family fallback (RFC).

maria.pm: thanks everyone. creating customer follow-up note and scheduling postmortem tomorrow 09:00 UTC. csm_linda will lead customer communication.
ajay.k: leaving note: if any regression, re-ping pagerduty.
carl.eng: logging final artifacts: routing traces, policy diff, queue purge logs, patch id 5f9b2, policy change at 1729457001.

tom.ops: 10m check-in: all looks stable. closing thread in 30m if no regressions.
